request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (50,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 26.8% (95% band 24.7% to 29.1%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.186: -0.8; 0.186 <= x < 0.328: -0.48; 0.328 <= x < 0.471: -0.22; 0.471 <= x < 0.599: +0.081; 0.599 <= x < 0.666: +0.68; 0.666 <= x < 0.709: +1.4; 0.709 <= x < 0.762: +2; x >= 0.762: +3.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.12, 95% band [+2.78, +3.36]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 16.2% (95% band 15.0% to 18.7%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.2; >= 2: +0.6 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.96, 95% band [+0.87, +1.01]).
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 8.7% (95% band 7.6% to 10.2%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 29,800: +0.39; 29,800 <= x < 45,000: +0.15; 45,000 <= x < 81,900: -0.104; x >= 81,900: -0.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.80, 95% band [-0.91, -0.60]).
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 7.3% (95% band 6.6% to 8.9%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 53.9: +0.32; 53.9 <= x < 190: +0.068; 190 <= x < 320: -0.14; x >= 320: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.60, 95% band [-0.74, -0.49]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 5.5% (95% band 4.7% to 6.3%); rank 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.434: -0.08; x >= 0.434: +0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.27, 95% band [+0.18, +0.41]).
- `num_dependents`: number of dependents (standardised).
  Share of importance 2.3% (95% band 0.6% to 3.0%); rank 6 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.25, 95% band [-0.29, +0.03]).
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 1.8% (95% band 1.2% to 2.6%); rank 6 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2: 0; >= 3: +0.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.18, 95% band [+0.08, +0.25]).
- `months_at_address`: months at the current address (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.7% (95% band 0.4% to 2.7%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.06, 95% band [-0.05, +0.16]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.2% to 1.5%); rank 8 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.02, 95% band [-0.09, +0.14]).

Interactions: the model has 35 pairs. The larger ones:
- `utilization & n_delinquencies`: share of importance 16.4% (95% band 14.5% to 17.5%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0978 to 0.749: +0.94 (95% band +0.78 to +1.24) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, +5.53 (95% band +4.64 to +5.73) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: -0.45 (95% band -0.56 to +0.04) when `utilization` = 0.0978, +4.14 (95% band +3.55 to +4.36) when `utilization` = 0.749.
- `history_months & n_inquiries`: share of importance 3.0% (95% band 1.8% to 3.7%).
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 342: -0.23 (95% band -0.47 to -0.11) when `n_inquiries` = 0, -1.26 (95% band -1.27 to -0.84) when `n_inquiries` = 4.
  Effect of `n_inquiries` from 0 to 4: +0.94 (95% band +0.42 to +0.90) when `history_months` = 23.5, -0.09 (95% band -0.27 to +0.02) when `history_months` = 342.
- `income & history_months`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.3% to 1.1%).
  Effect of `income` from 21,900 to 114,000: -0.77 (95% band -0.97 to -0.54) when `history_months` = 23.5, -0.58 (95% band -0.88 to -0.39) when `history_months` = 342.
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 342: -0.68 (95% band -0.91 to -0.43) when `income` = 21,900, -0.49 (95% band -0.75 to -0.36) when `income` = 114,000.
- `utilization & history_months`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.6% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0978 to 0.749: +2.97 (95% band +2.64 to +3.26) when `history_months` = 23.5, +3.17 (95% band +2.81 to +3.41) when `history_months` = 342.
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 342: -0.65 (95% band -0.88 to -0.48) when `utilization` = 0.0978, -0.44 (95% band -0.65 to -0.33) when `utilization` = 0.749.
- `utilization & income`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.5% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0978 to 0.749: +3.06 (95% band +2.62 to +3.34) when `income` = 21,900, +3.05 (95% band +2.82 to +3.44) when `income` = 114,000.
  Effect of `income` from 21,900 to 114,000: -0.82 (95% band -1.04 to -0.55) when `utilization` = 0.0978, -0.83 (95% band -0.91 to -0.48) when `utilization` = 0.749.
- `income & dti`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.2% to 1.2%).
  Effect of `income` from 21,900 to 114,000: -0.81 (95% band -0.93 to -0.58) when `dti` = 0.0295, -0.96 (95% band -1.03 to -0.63) when `dti` = 0.571.
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0295 to 0.571: +0.38 (95% band +0.17 to +0.57) when `income` = 21,900, +0.24 (95% band +0.15 to +0.40) when `income` = 114,000.
- `n_delinquencies & history_months`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 0.9%).
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.92 (95% band +0.82 to +0.98) when `history_months` = 23.5, +0.99 (95% band +0.89 to +1.07) when `history_months` = 342.
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 342: -0.64 (95% band -0.76 to -0.50) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, -0.57 (95% band -0.71 to -0.47) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
- `n_delinquencies & income`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.2% to 1.0%).
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.90 (95% band +0.78 to +0.99) when `income` = 21,900, +1.06 (95% band +0.89 to +1.09) when `income` = 114,000.
  Effect of `income` from 21,900 to 114,000: -0.84 (95% band -0.94 to -0.63) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, -0.68 (95% band -0.82 to -0.53) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
- `dti & num_dependents`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 0.7%).
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0295 to 0.571: +0.24 (95% band +0.17 to +0.49) when `num_dependents` = -1.64, +0.34 (95% band +0.19 to +0.44) when `num_dependents` = 1.63.
  Effect of `num_dependents` from -1.64 to 1.63: -0.27 (95% band -0.29 to +0.06) when `dti` = 0.0295, -0.17 (95% band -0.36 to +0.08) when `dti` = 0.571.
- `months_at_address & num_dependents`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 0.9%).
  Effect of `months_at_address` from -1.66 to 1.65: -0.06 (95% band -0.21 to +0.19) when `num_dependents` = -1.64, -0.01 (95% band -0.22 to +0.17) when `num_dependents` = 1.63.
  Effect of `num_dependents` from -1.64 to 1.63: -0.30 (95% band -0.32 to +0.13) when `months_at_address` = -1.66, -0.25 (95% band -0.32 to +0.03) when `months_at_address` = 1.65.
- 25 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 4.2%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by revolving credit utilization, which accounts for about 27% of the model's importance, and its effect rises steeply once utilization passes roughly 0.6 of the credit limit."},{"id":2,"text":"The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver (about 16%): having two or more raises the predicted risk noticeably compared with none."},{"id":3,"text":"Income, length of credit history, and debt-to-income ratio matter less: lower income and shorter credit histories push predicted risk up, and a debt-to-income ratio above about 0.43 adds some risk."},{"id":4,"text":"The strongest interaction is between utilization and delinquencies: high utilization matters far more for applicants with delinquencies (about +5.5 on the log-odds scale across the utilization range) than for those without (about +0.9)."},{"id":5,"text":"A second notable interaction pairs credit history length with recent inquiries: many inquiries raise risk mainly for applicants with short histories, and the effect largely disappears for those with long histories."},{"id":6,"text":"Number of dependents, months at address, and age show effects the data do not reliably distinguish from zero, so they should not be read as drivers of default."},{"id":7,"text":"The smaller interactions involving income and history length are real but modest, and the data are not precise enough to rank them confidently against each other."}]}
